page: Amazon Web Services g5g.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and designed around the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores via the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. System memory is configured at 128 GB, equating to 2.0 GB per physical core. Graphical and compute acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA T4G GPUs based on the Turing architecture, providing a total of 32 GB of video memory. The platform includes a 25 Gbps baseline network interface and includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage volumes for file systems.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance characteristics driven by core density and memory caching. The 64 dedicated ARM cores achieve strong results in multi-core compute tests, including top-quartile performance in stress-ng multi-core and Clang software compilation. Cached small-block memory reads, static web serving throughput reaching 44.64 GB/sec, and Redis operations exceeding 76 million operations per second similarly benchmark in the top quartile. Conversely, per-core performance is limited, with Geekbench single-core, text processing, and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom quartile. Machine learning inference displays acceptable prompt processing speeds on small to medium models, but token generation for 70B parameter models is constrained.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance delivers high compute and memory efficiency per thread by utilizing non-hyperthreaded Graviton silicon paired with dedicated GPUs. The lack of local storage requires persistent data to traverse network storage layers, which should be accounted for in I/O planning. This platform is suited for multi-threaded build systems, Android cloud gaming and graphics streaming, small-to-medium deep learning inference, and high-concurrency caching services.
description: Amazon Web Services g5g.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, integrating 64 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz with two NVIDIA T4G GPUs delivering 32 GB of combined VRAM. Memory capacity is allocated at 128 GB, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU across the ARMv8 architecture, while baseline network throughput reaches 25 Gbps. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Benchmark measurements indicate robust multi-core compute and compilation capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core tests and Clang compilation ranking in the top quartile. It also demonstrates high throughput in Redis operations and static web delivery. However, single-threaded throughput shows lower relative speed in Geekbench and compression tasks, and large-scale language model generation remains constrained. This configuration fits GPU-accelerated Android game streaming, machine learning inference, multi-threaded builds, and high-throughput microservices.
